CitiCorp Interview Experience
Prasad Thakare    |    Computer Engineering    |    2019-2023
Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, all of our interviews for internship programs
were being held online. The test was held on the AMCAT platform and
interviews were conducted on Zoom.
Online Test (Around 2.5 - 3 hours)
The test had 4 sections:
●Technical MCQs
●Logical reasoning and basic maths MCQs
●English MCQs
●2 Coding Questions
First section consisted of only programming and DSA based MCQs.
Each section was individually timed (25 to 30 mins) and most of the
questions were easy. Free navigation was restricted in all the MCQ sections,
which means once a question is submitted, you cannot come back to it, also
you cannot randomly solve any question in the ongoing section.
I was able to solve almost all of them.
The coding section was 1hr long and everyone had received different
questions. Mine were:
●Printing a trapezium pattern of numbers
●Rat in a maze: Basically, given a maze represented by a matrix M,
where M[i][j] = 0 means the cell cannot be traversed, M[i][j] = 1 means it
can be traversed and M[i][j] = 9 means a piece of cheese is kept at that
position.
A mouse is present at M[0][0] and we must return true/false based on
whether the mouse can reach the piece of cheese.

I used simple DFS traversal considering the matrix as a graph.
I was able to solve both the questions fully and thus was selected for
the interview rounds which were held 2 days later. Total 41 students
were shortlisted.
Interview Round (on Zoom)
Round 1 (Technical, 20-30 mins)
The interviewer was very friendly and started by first asking me to introduce
myself and then asked me about my hobbies. After a few minutes he started
with the technical questions. He asked me the following questions based on
OOPS in C++, which was my preferred language.
1) How would you implement an interface in C++ ?
2) What is the use of an interface, how and where have you implemented it
? I explained this question with the help of an example and he seemed
satisfied with the answer.
3) What is polymorphism and its types?
4) Have you ever made use of function overloading in your projects?
Looking at my projects, he then proceeded to ask me about the frameworks
I’ve worked with in javascript. I said that I have some experience in React,
and these were the questions
1) How would you pass data between components in React ? My answer
was using props. He didn’t seem fully satisfied and proceeded to ask
further.
2) Have you worked with React Store ? I was not aware of this and thus
politely declined.
3) What is a state and how have you used them ? I was able to answer this
correctly and gave an example.
1

Further he went on to ask me what all data structures I was comfortable
with. I listed a few (including trees, coz I like trees XD).
1) First question was to find the kth node from the end in a linked list given
only the head pointer. I gave a naive and an optimized solution for this
problem.
2) Second question was, given an array A and an integer X, find the number
of pairs in A that sum up to X. I was able to give a naive and an optimized
solution for this too. He then asked me for an approach without sorting
and time complexity of each approach.
I was able to answer all the DSA questions correctly. He didn’t ask me to
code any of them. In the end he asked me whether I had any questions for
him, to which I asked him about the technologies we get to work with and
the cloud infrastructure at citi. Around 23 were shortlisted for the next round.
Round 2 (Technical+HR, 10-15 mins)
This interview was taken by a senior person from the company. He first
looked at my resume and said that he was amazed to see Kotlin there.
1) Why and how did you learn Kotlin ?
2) Have you worked with Mongo ? Why did you choose a NoSQL DB?
3) What qualities are necessary to become a software engineer?
4) Have you worked with oop ? Why do we use oop ?
5) Tell me about your parents and background.
6) Where do you see yourself in 5 years ?
7) What is your favourite technology ? Why ?
8) What do your peers and parents think about you ?
In the end he asked whether I had any questions ? I specifically asked about
java and where all it is used at citi.
2

Finally in the evening, the results were out and 10 students were selected in
total and I was one of them!
Advice:
1) Prepare your intro and the question you wanna ask the interviewer
beforehand.
2) For the coding round, consider going through the archives on gfg.
3) Be calm and answer confidently. If you are not aware of any
terminology which the interviewer asks you about, you can politely
decline / let him know that you are not sure before giving a final
answer  / if you can’t remember the exact definition, consider
explaining with the help of an example.
4) It is always important that you have a good understanding of your
projects and the technologies you have used for the same, along with
the reason why you chose to use that technology. Eg: why mongo ?
Why react ? etc etc.
5) You may get questions such as….what services does Citi (company
dependent) offer?
So it’s better to have a little bit of background knowledge about the
company
Feel free to reach out and Best of Luck!!
3
